The U720Li and TMW alloy ingots were made using vacuum induction melting.
The ingots were hot extruded successfully into v22-mm billets with extrusion ratio of 12:1 at about 1170 °C.
Before hot rolled, the ingots were soaked at 1149 °C for 12 h.
The final hot rolling reduction of 75% (from 50.8 to 12.7 mm) was reached by rolling two passes at about 1100 °C with InterHeat at 1121 °C for 30 min.
The rolled plates were subjected to the heat treatment (1100 °C/4 h/air cooling (AC), then aging at 650 °C/24 h/AC followed by 760 °C/16 h/AC).

The annealing twin length per unit area in TMW-4M3 is two times longer than that in U720Li.
In our previous study, a high density of annealing and deformation twins were observed in TMW-4M3 alloy.
The filtered HRTEM image, Fig. 2(b), clearly illustrates the SF existing between the two partials.
By substituting the corresponding values, the SFE of c matrix in TMW-2 from Fig. 2 is calculated to be 24.8 mJ/m2.
The final average SFE of c matrix in TMW-2 is 23.4 6 3.1 mJ/m2.
Initially, the SFE decreases with increasing Co and reaches the lowest value, which is 19.9 6 2.5 mJ/m2 in the c matrix of TMW-4M3 alloy with Co content of 34.0 at.%
Usually in the fcc c phase, a dislocation with Burgers vector of a/2 <110> can split into two Shockley partials with a stacking fault (SF) between them, which is called an extended dislocation.
Low SFE promotes the dissociation of perfect dislocations and facilitates the twin nucleation, resulting in high density of twins.
We have suggested twin strengthening contributes greatly to the improved mechanical properties.
